rows.answer:

Eagle's landing on 1969-07-20 is in [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The command and service module was built by North American Aviation. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The investigating board, the Apollo 13 Review Board chaired by Edgar Cortright, traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not state in a fact line that the board named the thermostatic switches as the start of the fire. The switch link appears only in note descriptions. The heater specification was revised to 65 volts in 1965 and the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: How long before Kennedy's speech at Rice University did NASA announce its Apollo mission mode?
rows.answer:
NASA announced lunar orbit rendezvous as the Apollo mission mode on 11 July 1962 [[lunar-orbit-rendezvous]] "[stated] NASA announced it as the Apollo mission mode on 1962-07-11 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

Kennedy gave the Rice University speech on 12 September 1962 [[john-f-kennedy]] "[stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The announcement came 63 days (about nine weeks) before the speech. This gap is my own calculation from the two dates.

rows.question: The landing site described in the Apollo 11 Mission Report's powered-descent section was named by an astronaut. What was first about the Gemini flight he commanded, and when was it?
rows.answer:
The landing site is Tranquility Base. Neil Armstrong named it at touchdown: [[tranquility-base]] "[stated] Named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: Houston, Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The powered-descent section of the Apollo 11 Mission Report covers the descent to that landing: [[apollo-11-mission-report-ch-05]] "[stated] The approach path led into a large crater, forcing an unplanned redesignation (src: Apollo 11 Mission Report p.5-4, 2026-10-24)".

Armstrong commanded Gemini 8. The first thing about that flight was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit, and it flew in 1966: [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The brain gives only the year, 1966. It does not give the month or day of the Gemini 8 flight.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot, caught German measles about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch. That exposure started the crew swap ([[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)").

The swap brought in Jack Swigert in place of Ken Mattingly. Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but he died before taking office ([[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)").

The brain does not say when or how he died, so those details are not in your brain.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:

[[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins, the command module pilot. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not say anything else about what Collins did during the landing. The landing itself was flown by Buzz Aldrin, the lunar module pilot, but the notes don't describe his actions during the descent.

rows.question: How long did the Apollo 11 crew spend on the lunar surface?
rows.answer:
Not in your brain. The notes give the landing and splashdown dates, but not how long the crew spent on the lunar surface.

What the notes do state:
- The lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility [[apollo-11]] "Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- Neil Armstrong first stepped onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC [[neil-armstrong]] "First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- The crew splashed down in the Pacific on 1969-07-24 [[apollo-11]] "Splashed down in the Pacific on 1969-07-24 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The missing piece is the time between liftoff from the surface and the lunar module's return, or the total moonwalk time. The Apollo 11 Mission Report chunk I opened covers only the powered descent (Section 5.3), so it does not give that figure.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The mailbox was an improvised adapter made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. Engineers devised it because the command module's lithium hydroxide CO2 canisters were square and the lunar module's sockets were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The square-versus-round canister detail is cited as follows. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not give the step-by-step construction or the exact dimensions.

rows.question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?
rows.answer:
The Cortright report, the June 1970 Apollo 13 Review Board report, called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The report recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The switch problem itself: the tank's thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)" The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts, but the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. Each quote is copied from an opened note's fact line, including its `[stated]` tag.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** A KSC management meeting decided the crew swap, and it was announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** The oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. The mission goal changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth, by a Mission Control abort decision. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew, having used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970 (day not recorded):** The Apollo 13 Review Board report, chaired by Edgar Cortright, was published. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
